resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS dates the station to 1829 (appropriation and building year per LighthouseFriends); the NRHP nomination and the keeper roster date the first light/keeper to 1830. Story presents both.
Record dates of 1868 and 1970 are the second tower and the move of the light to a skeleton tower, not the first lighting.
NRHP gives 74 ft, USLHS 73 ft; the record gives 18.9 m which matches neither.

notes_for_editor: Source count is thin on primary records: the Light-House Board reports for 1867-68 and the 1905 siren are not in the corpus, so building and siren facts rest on LighthouseFriends and the NRHP form. The Light-House Board listed the station under New York in the 1890s, the Commissioner under Connecticut after 1915. The fog-signal hours are from the 1893 and 1900 volumes; the fiscal year of each was not confirmed. Heizman rescue is the Commissioner report for fiscal 1921 (scan p.664, printed page not confirmed). The 1913 September Usinger entry and 1926 Iten entry come from OCR-damaged bulletin text. The Brennan name and the "torn and angry water" quote are LighthouseFriends quoting the New York Evening Post of 31 March 1926; the paper was not read. Keeper roster (cite 4) copied from USLHS; USCG personnel set as role crew. Current status of the Coast Guard light and the ferry rules come from LighthouseFriends and should be checked against the Town of Greenwich. A newspaper search (Chronicling America) did not complete in time.
